HI! its me again ... this time i want to learn how to disable workspace. Im running linux mint mate 17.2 64bits. searched the web and found NO tutorial on how to disable this... i dont know why workspace exist anyway aside of grinding my perfomance

edit : thanks people i got it :)
how do i disable the god damn workspace ?

I think workspaces only hide windows that are in other workspaces, meaning that if you don't use other workspaces there shouldn't be any performance loss... You can get 'rid' of them, but AFAIK workspaces are built in the DE/WM, so completely removing that feature is not a possibility right now. What I can suggest though, would be to go in your settings, find the settings-menu for Workspaces (Not a mint user) and set the number of workspaces to the minimum value. Then get rid of the Workspaces widget in your Bar and you should be 'free' from (the pretty useful feature that is: )Workspaces! ;)

I find them useful when I have to use way too many programs at the same time.
I use one workspace for Internet browsing, Music player and watching movies,
another for hobbies/semi-serious stuff (Coding, Modeling, Drawing)
and use a last one where I leave windows from progams I leave in the background (Rendering Blender, Video Converter, term with bash script)
This way I don't have to go through 15 windows everytime I try to do something, but only the 3-4 related to what I am doing.
as im getting older i do less and less on my pc ... now its just a game console/media player/web browsing machine :)
In what way is it grinding your performance, if I may ask?
i read that somewhere on a linux forums .. and i find it logic .. more then one workplace should use more ressource ?

Well, consider what a workspace is, it's information where sets of windows are located on a screen and a way to switch between them. If we're going to have let's say 15 processes running at once those processes will use the same cpu regardless of if Xorg is currently showing them or not, so the only extra information needed for workspaces is references to position, which is extremely cheap in terms of resources. It's not like you have several Xorg servers running parallel for each workspace. If you want, run top or htop and compare. If you're concerned about this level of optimization, Linux Mint is not the distro you want :)
